correctness.rationale: The disjoint splitting↔outdegree≤1 edge-orientation correspondence is bijective. In connected trees, summing outdegrees leaves exactly one root and yields exactly v root-directed orientations. In unicyclic components all outdegrees equal one; two directed cycle choices uniquely force branches; excess-edge components have none. Hence the product count. Integer-break bounds every component weight by vertex order; balanced pairs of three-vertex paths plus a two/four-vertex path attain it for all d. Partial-function intersection events force matchings, giving exact inclusion-exclusion for total witness count. Bipartite rooted-tree/cycle species yield the stated bivariate EGF. The actual standalone checker independently enumerated 682 teams through 3×3 by raw partitions and each of 65536 teams at 4×4 by components, with random brute checks.

value.rationale: Irredundant splitting witnesses are the distinct nonredundant explanations of a disjunctive functional-dependence claim. Even though model-checking is decidable in logspace, a team may admit exponentially many explanations. The theorem gives an exact per-instance counting algorithm, a sharp maximum over all fixed-size value domains, a complete two-parameter aggregate count and a structural generating function, all grounded in the same natural invariant. It distinguishes multiplicity of explanations from mere satisfiability and identifies the precise forest extremizers. This is an exact motivated classification, not just a tiny numerical improvement or an arbitrary parameter slice.
